TITLE: A Note on Adverse Costs Awards Against Self-Represented Litigants
AUTHOR: T. Okonkwo
SOURCE: (2021) 44 Man. L.J. 88
YEAR: 2021

Self-represented litigants make up a growing share of civil proceedings in Canadian courts.1 Costs jurisprudence developed with represented parties in mind does not translate cleanly to this context.2 Courts have adopted inconsistent approaches to adverse costs awards against self-represented litigants who conduct their own litigation poorly but in good faith.3 A more principled framework would distinguish between poor advocacy and bad-faith conduct when assessing costs.4

1. Statistics Canada, Legal Problems and Access to Justice in Canada, 2021.
2. Fellowes, McNeil v Kansa General International Insurance Co, 1998 CanLII 5905 (Ont Sup Ct).
3. Jonsson v Lymer, 2020 ABCA 167.
4. See also Pintea v Johns, 2017 SCC 23.
